description_full: Zoar Limited, a pharmaceutical company, engages in the development, manufacturing, and distribution of pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and intermediates in Africa, the Middle East, India, Central and South America, Asia, and Europe. The company offers APIs for oncology, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, diabetes, central nervous system disorders, and neurological disorders. It also provides drug contract development and manufacturing services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. The company was founded in 2012 and is headquartered in Hung Hom, Hong Kong.
financial_summary: Zoar Limited is a small-cap healthcare business with a $479M market cap on $652M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 22% against a 9% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 17% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $623,000 in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.01×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
Accruals are elevated at +13.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
